description: 31-question gold standard benchmark for PV AI Workbench retrieval validation. source_notes (list) accepted per question; any match in top-5 counts as hit.
scoring: precision@5 (source note in top 5 retrieved chunks) and MRR (mean reciprocal rank)

questions.question: What are the four criteria that make an ICSR a minimum valid case under ICH E2A?
questions.answer_key: Identifiable patient, suspect medicinal product, suspect adverse reaction, identifiable reporter

questions.question: What are the ICH E2A seriousness criteria for an adverse event?
questions.answer_key: Death, life-threatening, hospitalization/prolongation, disability, congenital anomaly, medically important

questions.question: What is the expedited reporting timeline for fatal or life-threatening unexpected SUSARs?
questions.answer_key: 7 calendar days for initial report, 8 additional days for follow-up

questions.question: How does ICH E2A define an unexpected adverse drug reaction?
questions.answer_key: Nature, severity, specificity or outcome not consistent with applicable product information

questions.question: What are the four components of the signal management process under EMA GVP Module VI?
questions.source_note: Guidelines/EMA GVP Module VI - Signal Management.md
questions.answer_key: Signal detection, signal validation, signal analysis and prioritization, recommendation for action

questions.question: How does EMA GVP Module VI define a pharmacovigilance signal?
questions.source_note: Guidelines/EMA GVP Module VI - Signal Management.md
questions.answer_key: Information suggesting a new potentially causal association or new aspect of a known association, judged of sufficient likelihood to justify verificatory action

questions.question: What data sources are used for signal detection according to GVP Module VI?
questions.source_note: Guidelines/EMA GVP Module VI - Signal Management.md
questions.answer_key: Spontaneous reporting systems, clinical studies, scientific literature, registries and databases, digital health data

questions.question: What does ICH E2E guidance say about the four components of pharmacovigilance planning?
questions.answer_key: Safety specification, pharmacovigilance plan, routine pharmacovigilance, additional pharmacovigilance activities

questions.question: What regulatory guideline governs individual case safety report data elements in electronic format?
questions.answer_key: ICH E2B(R3) — Clinical Safety Data Management: Data Elements for Transmission of Individual Case Safety Reports

questions.question: What are the key differences between E2B(R2) and E2B(R3) formats?
questions.answer_key: E2B(R3) uses HL7 ICSR v3 XML schema; adds structured data for medical history, lab data, and improved narrative fields

questions.question: What are the Evans criteria for a positive PRR signal?
questions.answer_key: PRR >= 2.0 AND N >= 3 AND chi-squared >= 4.0 (all three must be met)

questions.question: How is the Proportional Reporting Ratio calculated?
questions.answer_key: (a/(a+c)) / (b/(b+d)) where a=drug+reaction cases, b=other drugs+reaction, c=drug+other reactions, d=other drugs+other reactions

questions.question: What does a PRR of 1.0 indicate?
questions.answer_key: Reaction is reported at the same rate as the background — no disproportionate reporting signal

questions.question: What is confounding by indication and why is it important for last-resort antibiotics?
questions.answer_key: Patients receiving last-resort drugs are inherently sicker, making mortality-related PRRs appear elevated without indicating a true causal signal

questions.question: What is the Weber effect in FAERS signal detection?
questions.answer_key: Reporting rates for adverse events tend to be highest in the first two years after drug approval and decline thereafter

questions.question: What is the masking effect (competition bias) in disproportionality analysis?
questions.answer_key: A very strong signal for one drug-reaction pair can suppress (mask) detection of weaker signals for the same reaction

questions.question: What is the MedDRA hierarchy from lowest to highest level of granularity?
questions.answer_key: LLT (Lowest Level Term) → PT (Preferred Term) → HLT (High Level Term) → HLGT (High Level Group Term) → SOC (System Organ Class)

questions.question: At what level of the MedDRA hierarchy are adverse events coded for regulatory reporting?
questions.answer_key: Adverse events are coded at the Preferred Term (PT) level for regulatory reporting

questions.question: How should 'drug didn't work' be coded in MedDRA?
questions.answer_key: Drug ineffective (PT) under SOC: General disorders and administration site conditions

questions.question: What is the difference between Anaphylaxis and Anaphylactic reaction as MedDRA PTs?
questions.answer_key: Anaphylaxis denotes the full clinical syndrome; Anaphylactic reaction may be used when the reporter describes a reaction without full diagnostic criteria being met

questions.question: What structure should an E2B(R3)-compliant ICSR narrative follow?
questions.answer_key: Patient demographics/history, drug exposure details, adverse event description and course, treatment/outcome, causality assessment

questions.question: When should a case be classified as unexpected in ICSR processing?
questions.answer_key: When nature, severity, specificity, or outcome is not consistent with the applicable product information (SmPC or IB)

questions.question: How is de-challenge documented in an ICSR narrative?
questions.answer_key: Document whether the adverse event resolved or improved following drug withdrawal, and the timeframe of resolution

questions.question: What seriousness criteria apply when a patient is hospitalized due to an adverse event?
questions.answer_key: Requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization — meets ICH E2A seriousness criterion

questions.question: What is the minimum recommended frequency of literature monitoring under EMA GVP?
questions.source_note: Guidelines/EMA GVP Module VI - Signal Management.md
questions.answer_key: Continuous monitoring with at minimum weekly review for key data sources

questions.question: What literature sources should be monitored for pharmacovigilance signals?
questions.source_note: Guidelines/EMA GVP Module VI - Signal Management.md
questions.answer_key: MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE, local literature, EMA communications, other regional databases

questions.question: How does literature monitoring contribute to the PSUR/PBRER?
questions.answer_key: Literature review findings are included in the safety evaluation section and may generate new signals requiring discussion in the PSUR benefit-risk evaluation

questions.question: What is signal validation in the context of GVP Module VI?
questions.source_note: Guidelines/EMA GVP Module VI - Signal Management.md
questions.answer_key: Evaluating whether examination of individual case reports and summaries provides sufficient grounds to recommend signal assessment

questions.question: Under what circumstances does a literature finding require expedited reporting?
questions.answer_key: Published case reports meeting SUSAR criteria (serious + unexpected) require expedited reporting within 15 days (or 7 days if fatal/life-threatening)

questions.question: What is the regulatory basis for requiring a Periodic Safety Update Report?
questions.answer_key: ICH E2C(R2) PBRER guideline — marketed products must submit periodic reports summarizing benefit-risk evaluation at defined intervals
source_notes: Guidelines/EMA/EMA GVP Module V - Risk Management Systems.md
Guidelines/EMA/EMA GVP Module VII - Periodic Safety Reports.md

questions.question: What methodological guideline is the PRR approach aligned with for signal detection?
questions.answer_key: ICH E2E Pharmacovigilance Planning — signal detection methodology section recommends quantitative statistical methods including PRR
